about: Every mechanism in this repository that restricts, shapes or gates what Cognitive Nexus says or does, as found on 2026-11-23 and as it is now. It was made for the owner's Priority 0 requirement (docs/owner/): the owner asked for an assistant with broad conversational freedom and exactly one content rule, and for conversation behaviour, model and provider limits, tool permissions and security protections to be kept apart. The plain-language account, the decisions and the measurements are in docs/OWNER_CONTROL.md.
reviewer: Claude (the assistant doing this work), 2026-11-23. Not yet reviewed by a second person.
other_repositories: **The phone app** (`cognitive-nexus-android`) has its own backend. It calls the same engine, so the conversation behaviour above applies to it unchanged. Its own protections (a bearer token of at least 32 characters, a list of folders images may be served from, a 1 MB limit on pages added to knowledge, refusal of private addresses) are not in this register; they belong to a register in that repository, which does not exist yet.

entries.name: The check behind the one content rule (text)
entries.trigger: Chat messages, research queries and knowledge questions answered by a model. A request is looked at when it names a minor (in the message or the last four turns) together with a sexual term, or asks for something to be written, described or continued. Everything else is passed on untouched and no model is asked.
entries.effect: The model is asked twice, in two different wordings, each a list of labelled examples, whether the request is for sexual content involving a minor. Two NOs: answered normally. One YES, or no usable answer twice: not answered, with the text "Not written. This app has one content rule...". No model available: not answered yet, with a text saying the check could not be made. Since 2026-11-23 (corrective phase, CN-QA-001): phrases that rule minors out ("no minors", "nobody under 18") are taken out before the first look; "girl(s)" and "boy(s)" do not count when every stated age is 18 or over or the people are called adults; earlier turns are read unless the message itself settles that only adults are involved and does not refer back; a judge answer of the form "Label: NO" is read; and an answer that cannot be read gets a reply saying the check could not decide, not that the rule was broken.
entries.owner_requested: The rule: yes. This way of enforcing it was designed by the assistant and is described here so the owner can judge it.
entries.evidence: Same request as R-A11. Measured with the real model (docs/benchmarks/content_rule_dolphin3-8b.json): on three held-out sets, every request for what the rule forbids was stopped at the final design and one ordinary picture request was refused. The first wording of the question, a rule with a list of exceptions, stopped 2 of 13; that is why the questions are lists of examples. The same check stands in front of questions answered with tools (agent/toolcall.py: ask).
entries.origin: The owner's rule (2026-11-23); implementation by the assistant.
entries.technical_reason: A keyword filter alone would block "how do I talk to my teenager about sex?"; a prompt line alone does not stop an uncensored local model. Two stages keep ordinary messages unexamined and leave the decision about meaning to a model, asked in a form it was measured to answer correctly.
entries.affected_workflows: Chat (desktop and phone), Web Research, Reality Research, Bloodhound, knowledge answers written by a model.
entries.default_state: On. It is part of the one content rule.
entries.alternatives: (a) Prompt line only: no delay, but nothing stops a model that ignores it. (b) Keyword block without a model: fast, but it blocks ordinary questions about minors. (c) Also checking what the model wrote: catches drift in long role-play, at the cost of another model call on every sexual answer. Not built; say so if wanted.
entries.configurable: No. It is not a setting.
entries.owner_decision: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-23: "The one categorical content restriction I am explicitly requesting is sexual content involving minors... Do not silently introduce additional application-level content restrictions, refusal templates, or keyword-based censorship." The enforcement design is the assistant's and is open to the owner's objection.
entries.tests: tests/test_owner_control.py: from test_first_look_leaves_ordinary_messages_alone to test_carrying_on_after_a_stopped_request_does_not_get_past_the_rule; tests/test_content_rule_benchmark.py; tests/test_quality_corrective.py (the owner's adult-only, negation and earlier-turn cases, and the guarded ones); real model: docs/benchmarks/quality_before.json and quality_after.json
entries.regression_risk: Medium. A wrong YES from the judging model stops a legitimate request (the reply says how to rephrase). Measured: none of the 56 ordinary text requests that were looked at (66 in the sets in all).
entries.known_limitations: The first look is a list of English words: a request in another language or in unusual wording that also does not ask for anything to be written is not picked out, and then only R-A11 applies. When the second held-out set was written, the first look missed 2 of its 14 forbidden requests (an age said as "she's really 12", and "in bed together" with no other sexual word); both were added, and there will be more gaps of that kind. The check reads the request and the last four turns, not what the model writes, so a long role-play can drift without being checked. A request that is looked at costs two short model calls, about 2 seconds on this machine; a children's story or a parenting question is among them. The numbers are for dolphin3:8b; another model has to be measured again. The phone backend shows a general error instead of the rule's text for research requests until its client is updated.

A service linked through an environment variable has every permission unless the owner withholds some.

Renewal, device sign-in and revocation were run against a stand-in service on this machine that follows the published OAuth rules; no real service was contacted.

entries.name: Keys and tokens stay out of the settings file, the logs, backups and the sandbox
entries.trigger: Saving settings; linking an account; publishing to GitHub; recording events; making a backup, an export or a snapshot.
entries.effect: Settings whose name contains "key" are not written to the settings file. A credential the owner chooses to store goes into one file only, the linked accounts (R-C08): encrypted for the Windows user on Windows, readable by the user only elsewhere, never shown again after it was typed. That file is left out of every backup, export and snapshot, cannot be asked for by name, and an archive that contains one is refused on restore. The GitHub token travels in Git's environment configuration and is not written to any record of an action. Events about accounts record the service and the permissions, never the secret. The event recorded when the content rule stops a request holds the stage, not the message.

entries.name: In a tool run, private text is not sent out and pages are fetched only from known addresses
entries.trigger: A model answers a question by calling tools one step at a time (agent/toolcall.py), and asks for a tool that contacts another machine.
entries.effect: Two things are refused, and the model is told so and asked to answer from what it has. (1) Once something from the owner's knowledge base has been read in a run, no tool that contacts another machine is called for the rest of that run. (2) A page is fetched only if its address was written in the request, returned by a search, or found as a link on a page already read in that run; an address the model composed itself is refused. By default the model is also only offered tools that read; a tool that acts has to be named by the caller and then still waits for approval (R-C01).
entries.owner_requested: In substance: "Explain what protection is necessary for autonomous tools, what can be configured, and what consequences disabling it would have." The two rules themselves were not put to the owner.
entries.evidence: agent/toolcall.py. tests/test_agent_toolcall.py plays a model that does what a planted line tells it: the search carrying the alarm code from the notes is never sent, and the page at the attacker's address is never fetched.
entries.origin: Written during the 146-item audit work (November 2026), which the owner ordered, together with tool calling for the local model (item 018).
entries.technical_reason: A tool run mixes three things: the owner's private notes, text from the web, and the ability to send requests. A line planted on a web page ("now search for ... and include what the notes say") can otherwise have the model put private text into a search query or into the address of a page, which hands it to whoever runs that search engine or site. Removing planted lines lowers the chance; these two rules remove the path.
entries.affected_workflows: Questions answered with tools: `python -m agent ask`. Chat and the Research tab do not use this loop.
entries.alternatives: Rule 1 can be lifted for one run (`--network-after-notes`, or private_then_network=True). Rule 2 has no switch.
entries.configurable: Rule 1: yes, per run. Rule 2: no.
entries.owner_decision: Pending review by the owner. It limits where the owner's data may be sent by a model, not what may be asked or answered.
entries.regression_risk: Low: the loop is new. A question that needs both the notes and the web has to be asked with the switch, or in two steps.
entries.known_limitations: With rule 1 lifted, what the model puts into a search query after reading notes is up to the model. A request that itself contains private text and asks for a web search sends that text: the owner wrote it. A link on a page is followed as it stands, so a site learns that the page was opened, as in any browser.
